## Research Focus

My scholarship examines the validity of inferences supported by quantitative evidence. This work connects four broad areas:

::: {.research-grid}

::: {.research-card}

### Latent Variable Modeling

Examining the estimation, evaluation, and interpretation of models involving constructs that cannot be observed directly.

:::

::: {.research-card}

### Psychometrics and Measurement

Studying how instruments and scores support conclusions about psychological and educational phenomena.

:::

::: {.research-card}

### Classification and Decision-Making

Investigating model-based classification, group enumeration, uncertainty, and the consequences of quantitative decisions.

:::

::: {.research-card}

### Validity and Evidentiary Reasoning

Evaluating how research design, measurement, analysis, and interpretation work together to support defensible conclusions.

:::

:::

[Explore the Research Program](research.qmd){.section-link}

## Selected Contributions

::: {.contribution-grid}

::: {.contribution-card}

### Categorical Latent-Variable Estimation

Research on the accuracy and performance of estimation methods under conditions commonly encountered in applied research.

:::

::: {.contribution-card}

### Latent Class and Profile Enumeration

Research examining how data characteristics affect decisions concerning the number and nature of latent groups.

:::

::: {.contribution-card}

### Model-Fit Evaluation

Research evaluating the performance of fit indices across a range of latent-variable models and analytic conditions.

:::

::: {.contribution-card}

### Consequential Inference

Emerging work examining how measurement, model choice, and analytic uncertainty affect consequential classifications and decisions.

:::

:::

## Recent Work

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| results: asis

homepage_publications <- read.csv(
  "assets/data/publications.csv",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
  check.names = FALSE
)

homepage_publications <- homepage_publications[
  order(homepage_publications$year, decreasing = TRUE),
]

homepage_publications <- head(homepage_publications, 3)

escape_home_html <- function(x) {
  x <- ifelse(is.na(x), "", x)
  x <- gsub("&", "&amp;", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub("<", "&lt;", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub(">", "&gt;", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub('"', "&quot;", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x
}

homepage_publication_cards <- vapply(
  seq_len(nrow(homepage_publications)),
  function(i) {

    pub <- homepage_publications[i, ]

    title_html <- escape_home_html(pub$title)

    if (
      !is.na(pub$doi_url) &&
      trimws(pub$doi_url) != ""
    ) {
      title_html <- sprintf(
        paste0(
          '<a href="%s" target="_blank" ',
          'rel="noopener noreferrer">%s</a>'
        ),
        escape_home_html(pub$doi_url),
        title_html
      )
    }

    sprintf(
      paste0(
        '<article class="home-publication-card">',
        '<div class="home-publication-topline">',
        '<span class="home-publication-year">%s</span>',
        '<span class="home-publication-type">%s</span>',
        '</div>',
        '<h3>%s</h3>',
        '<p class="home-publication-authors">%s</p>',
        '<p class="home-publication-source"><em>%s</em></p>',
        '</article>'
      ),
      escape_home_html(pub$year),
      escape_home_html(pub$publication_type),
      title_html,
      escape_home_html(pub$authors),
      escape_home_html(pub$journal_or_publisher)
    )
  },
  character(1)
)

cat(
  '<div class="home-publication-grid">',
  paste(homepage_publication_cards, collapse = "\n"),
  '</div>'
)
```

## Collaboration and Engagement

The strongest methodological collaboration begins early, when measurement, design, and analysis can be developed together.

I contribute to research and grant projects through methodological leadership, measurement planning, statistical analysis, evaluation, validity review, speaking, workshops, and advisory service.

[Discuss an Engagement](engagement.qmd){.btn .btn-primary}

## Teaching, Mentoring, and Research Leadership

My mentoring uses a progressive apprenticeship model to help students develop from observers and contributors into independent scholars and methodological collaborators.

My research leadership focuses on building the systems, incentives, infrastructure, and capacity that allow scholars and institutions to pursue ambitious research goals.
